answer.text: cannot make fatty acids and must be handed them
answer.line: Paragraph 7: arbuscular fungi cannot make their own fatty acids and must be handed them by a host. That is largely why.

steps: Read the start of that sentence. They "cannot manufacture their own fatty acids and must be handed them by a host."
The word which ties that gap to the plate result. The gap is making, not storing.

choices.text: can store lipid only while it is attached to a living root
choices.note: Vesicles store lipid, paragraph 3, but storage is not the problem. The gap is making fatty acids at all.

choices.text: loses the ability to take up phosphate when no root is present
choices.note: Nothing ties phosphate uptake to a root being present.

choices.text: needs a mantle of root tissue in order to produce its spores
choices.note: A mantle belongs to the other partnership, paragraph 4, and it is fungal tissue, not root tissue. Spores appear only in paragraph 13.

choices.text: cannot make fatty acids and must be handed them
choices.note: Sentence 4: cannot manufacture their own fatty acids and must be handed them by a host.

choices.text: depends on carbon dioxide that living roots release into soil
choices.note: Respired carbon dioxide is in paragraph 12, as a route a label can take. It is never something a fungus must be fed.
